strengths: Addresses genuine gap in TTA evaluation: systematic exposure that state-of-the-art offline methods fail under realistic latency constraints that practitioners care about
Comprehensive and well-motivated framework: three temporal scenarios (discrete, continuous, amortised) thoughtfully cover distinct deployment patterns with concrete real-world examples

Clear mathematical formulation with interpretable decompositions: utility metrics cleanly separate contributing factors (availability×accuracy, alignment terms, adapted vs frozen phases), enabling diagnosis of failure modes
Extensive empirical validation: 240 scenarios (16 temporal × 15 corruptions) with concrete quantitative findings (ETA loses in 41.2% of cases; rank correlation rs ranges -0.74 to 0.21)

Significant findings: demonstrates rank instability is pervasive and corruption-dependent, revealing that temporal pressure triggers different failure modes (availability collapse, accuracy erosion, unproductive overhead)

Improvements over prior work justified clearly: addresses limitations of Alfarra et al. (2024) through buffering, single-model realism, and evaluation of continuous/amortised scenarios absent from prior work
Excellent presentation: clear writing, compelling motivation, effective visualizations (Figure 3 heatmaps), comprehensive appendices with method details and per-corruption analysis
Honest limitations discussion: transparently acknowledges scope to ImageNet-C/ResNet-50, episodic evaluation, method-evaluation mismatch (LAME underperforms by design), and excluded method families
weaknesses: Limited generalization scope: single dataset (ImageNet-C), architecture (ResNet-50), hardware (GPU), and task (classification). Claims extension is 'readily possible' but unvalidated; no evaluation on medical imaging, segmentation, or edge devices where latency constraints matter most

Arbitrary parameter choices without sensitivity analysis: T ∈ {50,100,200,400,1000}ms grounded in Nielsen HCI research but domain-dependent and unvalidated in TTA context; ρ values lack ablation; λ=39.9ms propagates through all scenarios without robustness study

Limited methodological novelty: individual components (availability metrics, temporal decay, budget constraints) are standard; novelty is in systematic combination rather than new methods, theory, or algorithms. Discrete protocol improvements over Alfarra et al. are incremental

Identifies problems without concrete solutions: three design properties (corruption-conditioned allocation, time-aware scaling, anytime performance) proposed but no algorithms, implementations, or new methods provided to validate these actually improve deployability

Statistical rigor below conference standards: single seed reported ('we report results for a single seed'), no confidence intervals despite acknowledged latency variance, no multi-run averages, no error bars in any table/figure

Discrete protocol lacks formal justification: recurrence relation (§3.1) is complex with no proof it correctly models the scenario; batch normalisation handling is subtle implementation detail affecting results but relegated to appendix without ablation studies

Reproducibility gaps: code repository mentioned as available in supplements but no link in main text; per-batch logs mentioned but not provided; GPU-specific timing won't reproduce on different hardware; hyperparameter versions for baseline methods unclear

Limited practical guidance: no clear methodology for practitioners to determine which temporal scenario applies to their system a priori, measure system parameters in the field, or adapt results to different batch sizes (evaluated at 64 only)
Offline aggregation unclear: Table 1 shows only 4 of 15 corruptions; full offline rankings relegated to appendix, making it harder to assess baseline instability in main text

Primarily diagnostic rather than constructive: contributes a useful evaluation framework but doesn't propose new TTA methods, advance theoretical understanding of why rank instability occurs, or provide concrete algorithmic solutions

strengths: Addresses genuine evaluation gap in TTA: conventional offline evaluation ignores latency constraints critical for real deployments; this is well-motivated and timely

Principled framework with sound mathematics: three scenarios grounded in deployment realities, utility metrics cleanly decompose into interpretable components (availability, responsiveness, frozen accuracy), enabling diagnosis of failure modes

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: 7 methods × 15 corruptions × 16 temporal scenarios (240 total) with careful implementation including 6σ latency provision and explicit timing decomposition into intrinsic/extrinsic overhead
Clear and compelling presentation: Figures 1-3 effectively communicate rank instability and temporal dynamics; notation well-documented; writing is accessible; strong motivation

Actionable insights: Identifies three failure modes (availability collapse, accuracy erosion, unproductive overhead) and corresponding design requirements (corruption-conditioned allocation, time-aware scaling, anytime performance) that provide concrete direction for method design

Honest treatment of limitations: Appropriately scopes claims to ImageNet-C + ResNet-50, acknowledges episodic evaluation mismatch for continual methods, doesn't over-generalise; transparency about methodology choices

Good reproducibility: Supplementary code with per-batch logs, clear hyperparameter documentation, thorough implementation details (Appendix B.3 on batch normalisation behaviour), fixed vs. measured latency choices

Methodologically sound refinement of prior work: Careful justification for revising Alfarra et al. (2024)'s discrete protocol with motivation in Appendix B; grounding of hyperbolic decay in HCI literature
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope: Single architecture (ResNet-50) and dataset (ImageNet-C); while authors argue principles generalise, direct evidence on vision transformers, mobile-optimised networks, or real-world datasets would strengthen claims and test framework extensibility

Somewhat expected findings: That slow methods struggle under temporal pressure is intuitive; quantifying across scenarios is valuable but lacks surprising insights that would reshape understanding of TTA or offline evaluation generally

Metric design choices partially unjustified: Hyperbolic decay κ = (1 + d/(T-λ))^{-1} motivated by HCI literature but specific parameterisation is somewhat arbitrary; no sensitivity analysis or comparison to alternative discount functions; T values chosen geometrically but rationale could be stronger

Single seed evaluation: Only one random seed reported; while latency variance is minimal (<1-4 ms), for primarily empirical contribution, multiple runs with summary statistics would strengthen confidence; per-batch logs available but limited

Incomplete solutions: Paper identifies problems (rank instability, three failure modes) but doesn't propose or evaluate solutions; corruption-conditioned allocation mentioned as necessary but not explored; leaves design direction implicit rather than constructive

Limited analysis depth: Documents rank instability occurs but provides limited investigation into why certain corruption-method pairs invert; correlation analysis is useful but deeper mechanistic understanding of feature perturbation characteristics would enhance insights

Discrete protocol modifications reduce comparability: Single-model buffered approach is more realistic but makes direct comparison with Alfarra et al. (2024) difficult; introduces non-standard protocol that may limit adoption

Method coverage gaps: Excludes recent multiple-forward-pass and wrapper-based methods for tractability, leaving contemporary progress partially unevaluated; LAME underperforms in all cases due to episodic/i.i.d. mismatch, reducing method diversity

strengths: Well-motivated framework addressing critical gap in TTA evaluation: conventional protocols ignore temporal constraints despite their importance in real deployments

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 750+ temporal evaluations across 11 methods, 15 corruptions, multiple datasets (ImageNet-C/V2/R), architectures (ResNet-50, ViT-B/16), and hardware platforms (GPU, CPU)

Methodologically sound: grounding in physical units (ms) rather than model-relative proxies is a significant improvement; discrete protocol revision addresses real limitations of Alfarra et al. (2024)
Decomposable utility metrics that isolate failure modes (availability collapse, accuracy erosion, harmful adaptation), enabling diagnostic understanding beyond simple accuracy numbers
Actionable findings: three necessary properties for deployable adaptation provide concrete design targets for future work
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (especially Figures 1, 3, 5); extensive reproducibility details and promised code release
Demonstrates generality through extended evaluation with different models, datasets, and hardware; findings are consistent across settings
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: framework is primarily careful engineering extending Alfarra et al. (2024); individual components (availability·accuracy, hyperbolic decay, weighted combinations) are straightforward rather than innovative

Methodological concerns: single-seed evaluation (2025) without confidence intervals; use of default hyperparameters for all methods could bias results; no exploration of whether rank changes reflect fundamental differences or hyperparameter mismatches

Design choices insufficiently justified: hyperbolic decay function not compared to alternatives; single-batch buffer arbitrary; specific parameter values (T, ρ, B) unmotivated by sensitivity analysis; no statistical significance testing of rank reversals

Scope limitations: episodic i.i.d. evaluation mismatches methods' designs (LAME fails 240/240 cases); evaluation restricted to Fully TTA, image classification only; findings may not generalize to continual streams or other tasks

Limited guidance on solutions: identifies three necessary properties but provides minimal concrete approaches; notes that corruption-difficulty estimation 'remains an open question,' leaving key design problems unresolved

Incomplete analysis of anomalies: SHOT-IM's frozen accuracy robustness explained plausibly but not rigorously validated; high variance in Spearman correlations (Std>0.4) not addressed with statistical testing
Hardware evaluation underdeveloped: Raspberry Pi results limited to single architecture/dataset; observation that winners differ by hardware not deeply explored, undermining generality claims

Presentation density: 36 pages with critical details (method descriptions, protocol comparisons) relegated to appendices; some notation introduced but underutilized (e.g., p_j in recurrence relations)
